result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both pages use beekeeping terms throughout and show a 12-hive overview. A's dropdowns start on Sunny, Queen Seen, Medium stores and Light pollen, so a quick save can record things the keeper never saw. B starts every dropdown on 'Not recorded', which is more honest and suits someone standing at a hive. Neither screenshot shows a save confirmation, and A's empty log just says 'No inspections recorded yet.' | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both forms use real beekeeping words (hive, queen, brood, stores, temperament, pests), and both stick to a single log page. A defaults its select fields to 'Not recorded', so nothing gets logged that the keeper didn't actually see. B pre-fills 'Seen', 'Calm', 'Sunny' and 'Medium', which can quietly save made-up observations, and its empty log says only 'No inspections recorded yet.' Neither screenshot shows the save confirmation, and A's log area is cut off, so its empty-state wording can't be seen and items 2 and 3 are partly guesses.
